sourceLabel: Audited consolidated financial results filed with the exchanges
coverage: Reported business segments · segment revenue before inter-segment revenue
definition: Each segment’s profit before finance costs, other unallocated income, the share of associates’ and joint ventures’ profit, exceptional items and tax. The rows add up to ₹2,893.2 crore, which becomes group profit before tax of ₹2,660.9 crore after those items. It is not profit after tax.
location: PDF page 13 (consolidated segment revenue and results, year ended 31/03/2026 column), PDF page 11 (consolidated results) and PDF pages 16–17 (consolidated note 9); the filing has no printed page numbers
notes: Source figures are in ₹ million and were divided by 10. Segment revenue of ₹25,428.7 crore is before ₹200.2 crore of inter-segment revenue; after it, revenue from operations is ₹25,228.5 crore. Total income, including other income of ₹191.6 crore, is ₹25,420.1 crore. Group profit after tax is ₹2,002.7 crore: profit before tax ₹2,660.9 crore less tax ₹658.2 crore. Of it, ₹1,941.7 crore belongs to owners of the company and ₹61.0 crore to minority owners of subsidiaries. Profit is after an exceptional item of ₹19.2 crore: higher gratuity (retirement pay for past service) and leave liability caused by the government’s new Labour Codes, which the company calls non-recurring and regulator-driven (note 9). Group profit also includes a ₹44.9 crore share of profit from associates and joint ventures. Apollo does not disclose profit for any single hospital, clinic or pharmacy.
insight: Hospitals bring in about half of the segment revenue and most of the segment profit. Pharmacy distribution brings in a little less revenue than hospitals but far less segment profit.
